label: Autexousion (Αὐτεξούσιον) - Christian Free Will
rationale: Richest and most complete autexousion node: full etymology, the Justin->Origen->Cappadocian evolution, the five doctrinal features, the libertarian/liberum-arbitrium reception note. Highest connectivity (53 in + 40 out = 93 edges, incl. 31 evidenced_by passage groundings). Chosen as the single canonical concept node for the Christian/patristic autexousion lexeme.

True duplicate. Same generic Christian autexousion concept (Irenaeus/Origen/Methodius/Gregory; same four-doctrine schema; same eph'-hemin contrast; same libertarian-reception caveat). Differs from canonical only by being shorter and tagged 'Roman Imperial' vs 'Patristic'. Period 'Roman Imperial' here is an artifact (2nd-4th c. CE Christian authors are conventionally bucketed Patristic). 40 inbound discusses/employs edges re-point to canonical.

has_variant_label: Autexousion as constitutive of human ousia (Methodius, De Autexousio)
rationale: Same concept (Christian autexousion as God-given self-determining power, image-of-God anthropology, dual good/evil capacity grounding moral agency). It is an author-specific elaboration, not a different concept. Merge into canonical but retain a 'has_variant' marker recording Methodius's distinctive ousia-not-accident framing.

has_variant_label: Autexousion as Peripatetic self-origination (Alexander of Aphrodisias, De Fato)
rationale: CAUTION: same lexeme (αὐτεξούσιον, αὐτο-+ἐξουσία, being the arche of one's own actions, broader than hekousion) but a PAGAN PERIPATETIC sense predating and feeding the Christian usage. Alexander's autexousion (De Fato 207, 233-235, 247) is the conceptual bridge from Aristotle's eph'-hemin to the Christian term. Recommended as a distinct sense node retained via 'has_variant' rather than a hard merge; if the curve must treat autexousion as one concept this alias collapses cleanly. Flagged for human review before any application.

has_variant_label: Formula 'eleutheron kai autexousion' (Theophilus Autol. II.27; Irenaeus Dem. 11)
rationale: This is the fixed patristic FORMULA ἐλεύθερον καὶ αὐτεξούσιον (earliest attested coinage of the doctrine, Theophilus II.27). Same concept as canonical autexousion but a distinct lexical unit and the historically earliest grounded attestation of the Christian doctrine. Preserve as a named variant so the formula-level provenance (Theophilus/Irenaeus, tlge_verified) survives the merge.

has_variant_label: Autexousion as immediate (Carneadean) evidence (Eusebius PE VI.6.21)
rationale: Passage-specific articulation: Eusebius posits autexousion as self-evident (enarges) like sensation, a Carneadean epistemic move (Amand p. 376). Same concept; preserve as variant to keep the distinctive 'free will as primary psychological datum, not syllogistic conclusion' sense and its PE VI.6.21 grounding.

has_variant_label: Basil's identification to eph' hemin = to autexousion (Hom. 'Quod Deus non est auctor malorum' 7, PG 31.345B)
rationale: CAUTION: dual-membership node. It is also a to-eph-hemin attestation. Its content is precisely Basil FUSING τὸ ἐφ' ἡμῖν with τὸ αὐτεξούσιον (PG 31.345B; Amand p. 393). Merging into autexousion is defensible (it asserts their identity) but it must be cross-listed under the to_eph_hemin concept too. Preserve as variant and add a cross-reference edge to concept_eph_hemin_in_our_power_aristotle_d4e5f6g7. Flagged for human review.
